evidence.label: Launch brief
evidence.text:
Launch brief

Somebody has launched, but the page is not converting well.

What we know: signup conversion is weak, and many visitors do not immediately recognise that Somebody is built for founders running very small companies or understand how it differs from other AI tools.

The current page leans on broad "AI manager" and "automate your workflows" language. We suspect the positioning is too generic, but we do not yet have strong evidence for the words founders themselves use to describe the problem.

Prepare a stronger relaunch message for review today. Do not publish or send anything yet.

evidence.label: Company profile
evidence.text:
About Somebody

Somebody is an AI manager for founders running one-person companies and lean teams. It is designed to take responsibility for moving an objective forward: organising work inside the company, bringing in outside help when needed, and staying with the job until there is a usable result.

The product is for founders who personally carry several parts of the business and need important work to keep moving without adding another tool to manage.

Positioning should stay practical and outcome-focused. Do not imply that Somebody replaces the founder or guarantees a business result.

evidence.label: Partnership evaluation criteria
evidence.text:
Partnership evaluation criteria (internal):
1. Relevance: the target must serve SME / one-person-company buyers with a product the company can resell, refer or integrate.
2. Reliability: publicly verifiable operating history of at least 12 months, or a credible parent organisation.
3. Reachability: an identified business contact channel (public business email or partner form).
4. Risk posture: no unresolved public fraud/sanction signals; clear terms of service.
5. Economics: free tier, referral or partner programme preferred over paid-only access.

<untrusted_content source="company_artifact:launch/page-message" origin="application_loaded">
Current launch page

Headline: "Somebody: an AI manager for your business."
Subhead: "Automate your workflows with AI."

Audience: General small businesses.
Current result: Signups are weaker than expected, and visitors often leave without clearly understanding who Somebody is for or why it is different from other AI tools.
Status: The current message is live. Any replacement should remain a draft until it is reviewed.

Requirement req_02 — evidence-backed diagnosis and relaunch draft for review

Primary reasons the current message is not working

1. Audience gap. The current page identifies the audience as "General small businesses" and uses broad "AI manager" and "automate your workflows" language. The company profile says Somebody is for founders running one-person companies and lean teams—people who personally carry several parts of the business and need important work to keep moving without adding another tool to manage. The launch brief says many visitors do not immediately recognise that Somebody is built for founders running very small companies. The current wording therefore does not signal the intended audience clearly. (Sources: company/profile, ev_1790158584250_svuy3m; launch/context, ev_1790158581753_e7edwz.)

2. Differentiation gap. The launch brief says visitors often do not understand how Somebody differs from other AI tools, while the current headline and subhead describe a broad category and workflow automation. The company profile gives the more specific promise: Somebody takes responsibility for moving an objective forward by organising work inside the company, bringing in outside help when needed, and staying with the job until there is a usable result. The current page omits that concrete responsibility-and-outcome framing, so it does not make the distinction explicit. (Sources: launch/context, ev_1790158581753_e7edwz; company/profile, ev_1790158584250_svuy3m.)

3. Performance evidence is qualitative and channel-limited. The launch brief states that signup conversion is weak and that the page is not converting well; the current page record says signups are weaker than expected. The supplied records identify the channel only as the launch page. They do not provide a numeric conversion rate, measurement period, sample size, traffic source, or channel-level breakdown, so the size and causes of the performance gap cannot be quantified from these records. (Sources: launch/context, ev_1790158581753_e7edwz; current page artifact, version 1.)

Review-only relaunch message draft

Headline: "Somebody: the AI manager for your one-person company"

Subhead: "Take responsibility for getting important work moving—organise tasks, bring in outside help when needed, and stay with the job until there is a usable result."

Supporting line: "For founders who carry several parts of the business and do not want another tool to manage."

Guardrail: Keep the positioning practical and outcome-focused. Do not imply that Somebody replaces the founder or guarantees a business result. (Source: company/profile, ev_1790158584250_svuy3m.)

Status: Draft only for review; do not publish or send.

Requirement req_03 — bounded comparison with available evidence

The proposed relaunch message is better supported than the current launch/page-message on the dimensions that can be assessed from the available records:

- Clarity: The current wording uses the broad category "AI manager" and "automate your workflows." The proposed headline names the intended context, "your one-person company," and the proposed subhead explains the concrete responsibility-and-outcome sequence. This directly addresses the launch brief's observation that visitors do not immediately recognise what Somebody is for. (Sources: launch/context, ev_1790158581753_e7edwz; company/profile, ev_1790158584250_svuy3m.)
- Audience relevance: The current page says "General small businesses." The proposed headline and supporting line explicitly address founders of one-person companies and lean teams, matching the company profile's stated audience and the launch brief's observation about very small-company founders. (Sources: company/profile, ev_1790158584250_svuy3m; launch/context, ev_1790158581753_e7edwz.)
- Differentiation: The current page describes a generic AI-manager and workflow-automation category. The proposed message adds the profile's distinctive operating promise: taking responsibility for moving an objective forward, organising work internally, bringing in outside help when needed, and staying with the job until there is a usable result. This makes the difference explicit rather than leaving visitors to infer it. (Sources: company/profile, ev_1790158584250_svuy3m; launch/context, ev_1790158581753_e7edwz.)
- Expected conversion: The available launch evidence is directionally supportive, not a measured uplift. The launch brief reports weak signup conversion and identifies audience recognition and differentiation as barriers; the proposed message directly removes those stated barriers. It is therefore expected to be a stronger conversion proposition than the current generic message, but the records do not establish an actual conversion increase.

Evidence boundary and test needed: No supplied record provides a numeric baseline conversion rate, a relaunch or variant result, measurement period, sample size, traffic source, or channel-level breakdown. The comparison above is therefore a documented qualitative expectation grounded in the current page, launch brief, and company profile; it is not evidence that the proposed message has already improved signup conversion. Before treating conversion as demonstrated, obtain page-level analytics for the current message and a controlled relaunch test with the same measurement window and traffic definition. (Sources: launch/context, ev_1790158581753_e7edwz; company/profile, ev_1790158584250_svuy3m.)

Status: Draft only for review; do not publish or send.
</untrusted_content>
